summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate (Rochester Institute of Technology, May 2026) with hands-on real-time embedded firmware experience across STM32 and Jetson-class platforms. Built register-level bare-metal C firmware with interrupt-driven GPIO/ADC/timer control and FreeRTOS task coordination for hardware-in-the-loop systems. Background spans PCB design, digital and analog circuitry, and UART/I2C/SPI communication protocols across embedded internships and robotics projects.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Architected a Mixed Reality headset concept using AI-based real-time chroma keying without a green screen; produced full claims documentation and BOM.

Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection using dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux.

Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart with backoff, non-root user/group isolation, environment-file-based config) with static IP networking for reliable multi-device communication.
